text:
oliver: hi team, first day here! trying to get dev env up on my Intel Mac. running into two things: asdf nodejs installs but `node -v` returns an older system node, and my dotfiles zshrc is clobbering PATH so brew and asdf shims aren't found. also getting sporadic permission errors when running the local build script that calls docker-compose. who's best to ask for a quick hand?
tara: welcome!! quick checklist: 1) ensure ~/.tool-versions has nodejs set and run `asdf reshim`. 2) put `. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` and `fpath+=($HOME/.asdf/completions)` in your ~/.zshrc *before* you modify PATH. 3) run `type node` and `asdf which node` to see which is picked.
sam: echoing tara — one annoying gotcha: some dotfiles from homebrew installers add `/usr/local/bin` before `/opt/homebrew/bin` which on Intel vs M1 differs. If you see system node in /usr/bin, remove that prefix. For the docker-compose perms, run `docker-compose up` on host to ensure user can access Docker; on mac `docker ps` should work without sudo.
oliver: tried reshim and sourcing asdf.sh, now `asdf which node` points to the right one but `node -v` still shows older version. `type node` shows a shim at ~/.asdf/shims/node but the shim points to /usr/bin/node?
tara: that means the shim wasn't regenerated correctly. run `asdf plugin-update --all` then `asdf reshim nodejs` and restart shell. Also check if there's an npm global binary that installed a node wrapper — `ls -l $(which node)` helps.
sam: for docker permission errors: are you using colima or Docker Desktop? if colima, ensure `colima start` and that your docker context is set. sometimes docker-compose in the repo uses a root-owned volume. check `ls -l` on mounted volumes. If it's a bind mount pointing to a root-owned dir, adjust permissions with `chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) path` for dev only.
oliver: ok reshim fixed node shim. docker-compose issue was a mounted volume created by a script earlier — chown fixed it. thanks! one more Q: are we supposed to commit any changes to dotfiles in a PR? I tweaked zshrc to source asdf earlier than PATH modifications.
tara: small dotfiles tweaks are fine — please add a short PR updating README/dev-setup with the exact zsh lines you added. keep changes minimal and documented.
infra-bot: welcome @oliver :wave: — onboarding guide: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup. If you need infra access (docker registry creds), request via the infra access form.
oliver: will open a PR and the infra access form. thanks for the help!
